source_claims.claim: Independent Gamma(alpha_i, beta) coordinate variables have the joint product Gamma law.
The normalized vector Y_i = X_i / sum_j X_j has the Dirichlet law with parameters alpha_i.
The normalized Dirichlet vector lies in the nonnegative affine simplex with probability one.
That affine simplex has zero ambient Lebesgue volume, giving the singular-support statement.
The lower-dimensional projection route is justified by a measurable-set COV/preimage lintegral identity for the projected normalization map.
The projected first n-1 coordinates have the displayed Dirichlet density measure of equation (1.4).
When n = 2, the first normalized Gamma coordinate has the Beta(alpha1, alpha2) law.
